title: Debugging with AI: Reading Errors and Tracebacks
concepts: reading a traceback from the bottom up
SyntaxError: Perhaps you forgot a comma?

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asha asked the AI to make her day report print No sales today. for 0 sales and to say exactly what it prints. The AI said it prints No sales today., but its check was if sales >= 0:, which is true for 0, so the program still divided by zero and crashed with ZeroDivisionError. if sales > 0: fixes it.

changes: try and except are left out, because they are taught in Chapter 22; the chapter fixes causes instead of catching errors.
Debugger tools are left out; print debugging works everywhere without setup.
The logic error adds the loop counter instead of the price, because Chapter 8 already showed a total reset inside a loop.

The AI section adds video-only verified files: ai_zero_crash.py (the report crashing on 0 sales), ai_test_one.py and ai_test_three.py (the AI's version tested with 1 and 3 sales), ai_fixed_one.py and ai_fixed_three.py (the fixed version tested again), ai_improve_debug.py (the AI's suggestion that leaves a debug line in the output) and ai_report_final.py (the final report).
tools/storyboard.py now also checks on-screen questions, quiz options and pause text for banned phrases and em dashes.
outstanding_issues: The error reports in the lesson show the short file name; on a learner's computer the full path to the file appears instead.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
